item.title: World Insights: U.S.-led coalition departure from Iraq -- end of old chapter, start of new game?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
BAGHDAD, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- The U.S.-led international coalition concluded its military mission to combat the Islamic State (IS) in Iraq on Wednesday, following a withdrawal from Iraq's Erbil Air Base. The pullout coincided with Iraq's Sovereignty Day, a celebration of national independence and dignity. The move ends a turbulent two-decade U.S. military presence defined by invasion, occupation, withdrawal, and redeployment, a cycle that fundamentally reshaped Iraq's destiny, fueled regional instability, and exacted a heavy toll on Washington itself. Analysts view the withdrawal as the outcome of U.S. strategic realignments and shifting regional dynamics, signaling the end of an old era and the start of a complex geopolitical reshuffle. FROM INVASION TO DEPARTURE "The orderly departure of coalition forces and equipment from Erbil Air Base marks the successful conclusion of the military mission that defeated IS in Iraq," the Pentagon's chief spokesman said in a statement on Wednesday. While media described the U.S. forces departure as low-profile, experts emphasize its deep historical resonance. In 2003, Washington invaded Iraq without UN authorization under the pretext of searching for weapons of mass destruction, toppling Saddam Hussein's rule and plunging the nation into chaos. When U.S. forces hastily withdrew in 2011 under domestic and diplomatic pressure, the resulting security vacuum enabled terrorism to spread, leading to the rise of the IS in 2014, which seized vast swathes of territory in Iraq. Washington then assembled an international coalition and returned to Iraq. Despite Iraq declaring victory over IS in late 2017, thousands of U.S. troops remained. Rising public and governmental demand for sovereign control led to a September 2024 agreement between Iraq and the United States formalizing the coalition's withdrawal timeline. Analysts note the pullout reflects pragmatic considerations for both sides. For Baghdad, it marks a transition from external reliance to sovereign security management. For Washington, the diminished IS threat, alongside frequent attacks on U.S. troops by pro-Iranian militias, reduced the military rationale for staying. The pullout also aligns with U.S. domestic electoral commitments to end "endless wars" and reallocate military resources. TRAUMA & CHALLENGES The U.S. invasion left deep scars. According to Statista, a global statistical database, from 2003 to 2021, about 209,000 Iraqi civilians died in wars and violent conflicts. About 9.2 million Iraqis became refugees or were forced to leave their homeland. In Fallujah, high rates of cancer and birth defects persist due to the past use of depleted uranium and white phosphorus munitions by U.S. forces. While Iraq framed the departure as a milestone for national development, structural security challenges remain in the war-torn country. Iraq is under great pressure from the U.S. administration to disarm Iran-backed Shiite militias, many of which are defying state efforts to bring them under control, creating potential instability in the country, said Jumaa Mohammed, a politics professor at Iraq's Tikrit University. Concerns are also acute in Iraq's semi-autonomous Kurdistan region, which has faced repeated strikes since the United States and Israel launched joint military actions against Iran in late February. Kurdish authorities fear that the security situation could become even more dire following the U.S. withdrawal as they view U.S. forces as a vital security counterweight. Furthermore, physical troop withdrawal does not mean an end to Washington's influence. Ding Long, a Chinese expert on Middle East affairs at Shanghai International Studies University, notes that the United States is shifting from direct military occupation to leveraged influence through bilateral security agreements, energy partnerships, and financial mechanisms. Notably, Iraq's foreign exchange earnings from oil exports have been deposited in accounts at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York since 2003, giving Washington lingering economic leverage with control over the actual supply of U.S. dollars, said Li Ruiheng, an expert at the Center for Middle Eastern Studies of Peking University. NEW REGIONAL SHUFFLE Regional analysts consider the departure a continuation of U.S. strategic contraction in the Middle East, with lasting geopolitical ramifications. The withdrawal of U.S. forces could create space for Iran to expand its regional influence. Iran has long viewed U.S. military bases in the Middle East as a major security threat. The U.S. withdrawal from Iraq, a country bordering Iran, will diminish American military deterrence in Iran's immediate vicinity and, in effect, create room for Iran to further extend its influence. Conversely, Washington may seek deeper security cooperation with Syria, which joined the anti-IS coalition last year, focusing on intelligence sharing and counter-terrorism to constrain pro-Iranian supply corridors, analysts said. Ultimately, Iraq's quest for strategic autonomy depends on internal governance and regional balance. Reconciling political factions, addressing Kurdish security concerns, integrating militias, and preventing an IS resurgence remain critical long-term tasks. Experts said that as the region seeks to cut back on foreign interference, it will take sustained regional dialogue and inclusive diplomacy to deal with the geopolitical fallout and security gaps left by the United States.■

item.title: Mu Xinyue becomes first female Asian Games esports gold medalist
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- China's Mu Xinyue became the first female athlete to win an Asian Games esports gold medal after China defeated Japan in the Identity V Asian Games Version final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Wednesday. China's Identity V squad consists of hunters Shi Xiangwei and Sun Le, and survivors Lu Shujia, Chen Mingming, Lu Yahui, Fan Siqi and Mu. Mu, whose in-game ID is "Tao Wan'an," is the only female member of China's esports delegation at the Games. The final was interrupted by a technical issue between the two halves of the fourth round, with play suspended for nearly 30 minutes before competition resumed. Esports made its Asian Games debut as a demonstration sport at Jakarta 2018 before becoming an official medal sport at Hangzhou in 2023. The number of medal events has increased from seven in Hangzhou to 11 at Aichi-Nagoya, with Identity V Asian Games Version making its Asian Games debut. Although esports events at the Asian Games are open to both male and female athletes, men continue to make up the overwhelming majority of registered athletes. According to registration data for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, more than 500 athletes were registered for esports, with only 14 of them women. China entered four of the 11 esports events at Aichi-Nagoya -- Naraka: Bladepoint, Honor of Kings, Game for Peace Asian Games Version and Identity V Asian Games Version. China won gold in Naraka: Bladepoint and Honor of Kings and silver in Game for Peace Asian Games Version before adding the Identity V gold on Wednesday, concluding its esports campaign with three gold medals and one silver. ■

item.title: National Day floral displays in festive Beijing tell tough past, promising future
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- A grinning "boy" in sleek VR goggles stretches out his arm, pointing a finger forward. The plant sculpture in central Beijing has become a popular photo spot, with visitors striking the same pose as the "boy" for the camera. The sculpture is one of 10 themed floral displays installed along a roughly 6-km stretch of Chang'an Avenue, Beijing's main east-west thoroughfare, ahead of the National Day holiday, which begins on Oct. 1. It continues a tradition that has lasted more than four decades. Remarkably, some of this year's installations have captured young visitors' attention, sparking lively discussion on social media. "It's so, so cute, especially considering he's entirely green," one Rednote user commented on the plant-sculpted "boy" wearing VR goggles and sporting a distinctly cheerful expression. Echoing this animated and geek-chic sculpture is a running humanoid robot with a green-grass body and metallic "joints," installed at another major intersection along Chang'an Avenue. "This year's National Day plant sculptures are so funny," wrote another on Rednote. "Is it because the post-2000 generation has taken over?" "The displays were designed to appeal to people of all ages," said Lan Hailang, chief designer of this year's National Day floral displays. However, efforts to engage younger generations are perhaps most evident in the fluffy, grass-covered "cats" installed across the capital ahead of the National Day holiday. People have been sharing photos of them and guides to their locations. Among them, a 3.5-meter-tall kitten, outside Chang'an Avenue, stands out for its lifelike appearance. Designers used buffalo grass to recreate its long, fluffy fur, said Li Mengyu, a member of the design team. Beyond their appeal to youngsters, the 10 floral installations along Chang'an Avenue, alongside the centerpiece of a giant flower basket at Tian'anmen Square, tell stories of the country's revolutionary history, showcase its technological progress and aspirations for the future, and offer glimpses into the everyday lives of its people. The displays feature themes ranging from new quality productive forces and harmony between people and nature, to urban renewal and the beautiful countryside. "In earlier years, the floral displays were mainly about creating a festive atmosphere and giving people something to enjoy," said Lan. "In recent years, they have also become a window into the country's development and people's lives." Starting from Jianguomen, visitors first encounter a display themed "Carrying Forward the Long March Spirit." This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. The Long March was an epic military trek from 1934 to 1936, during which the Communist Party of China-led Red Army broke through encirclement by the Kuomintang forces. Red Army soldiers braved raging rivers, snow-covered mountains and treacherous grasslands, with some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers. The maneuver helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. Ninety years on, the spirit of the Long March remains a source of inspiration for many Chinese, reminding them to tackle difficulties head-on. "Compared with the formidable obstacles Red Army soldiers encountered during the Long March, many of the challenges we face in everyday life seem no big deal," said Zhang Caimeng, who traveled from Tianjin to Beijing ahead of the National Day. Standing before the display, she tried to inspire her son, who is preparing for next year's college entrance examination. Farther west, at the bustling commercial hub of Dongdan, the displays at four corners of the intersection feature technological achievements, including the Tiangong space station, a reusable rocket, a sprinting humanoid robot and a CR450 high-speed train. For more than 40 years, floral displays have been a prominent feature of National Day celebrations along Tian'anmen Square and Chang'an Avenue. The first flower display appeared in Tian'anmen Square in 1984. More than four decades later, the simpler flower arrangements of the early years have evolved into large-scale three-dimensional installations. The varieties of plants used have grown tremendously. Some of the displays are so exquisitely crafted that they too have become social media hits. One features a garland-wearing girl playing the violin, surrounded by black storks, red-crowned cranes and milu deer, creating a vivid scene of harmony between people and nature. The hem of the girl's floor-length gown is made up of brightly colored flowers. Her posture, the position of her bow and even the placement of her fingers on the strings are rendered with striking precision. A musical staff woven into the display spells out the beloved melody of "My Motherland and I," adding an unexpected touch that has delighted visitors and social media users alike. The display is more than a visual spectacle. At scheduled times, a recording of the violin solo "My Motherland and I" fills the air, drawing visitors to stop, film the scene and take in the experience. Li Lifang, an executive of the Beijing urban construction, landscaping and horticulture company, has been involved in building National Day floral displays for more than two decades. She said that while floral sculptures once depended heavily on the skill of artisans and craftsmen, technologies such as 3D modeling and simulation have made it possible to achieve greater precision and realism. For 29-year-old resident Hou Yueru, the displays depict scenes that feel close to home. Cycling along Chang'an Avenue, she was struck by the variety of scenes, from a kitten nestled in a rural setting and people paddleboarding along a waterfront, to community gardens and digital cultural and tourism experiences. "There are cutting-edge innovations that reach into the sky and deep underground, but there are also scenes that reflect the everyday lives of ordinary people," she said. Future aspirations are also woven into the plant sculptures. This year marks the beginning of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). The 18-meter-tall flower basket at Tian'anmen Square contains 15 types of plant-assembled "flowers" and five types of "fruit," symbolizing hopes for abundant blossoms and fruitful results during the five years. At Fuxingmen, the display titled "Forge Ahead" features galloping horses above the words "Strive ahead in the 15th Five-Year Plan period, work hard to open up new horizons," symbolizing a vigorous start to the new five-year period and the determination to pursue high-quality development through hard work. ■

item.title: Xi pays tribute to national heroes on Martyrs' Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Chinese President Xi Jinping straightens the ribbon on a flower basket during a ceremony to present flower baskets to fallen national heroes at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. Xi Jinping and other leaders of the Communist Party of China and the state including Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attended the ceremony on Wednesday. The event was held to mark Martyrs' Day. Observed on Sept. 30, one day before National Day, the day commemorates those who gave their lives for national independence and prosperity. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and other Party and state leaders attended a ceremony to present flower baskets to fallen national heroes at Tian'anmen Square in central Beijing on Wednesday morning. The event was held to mark Martyrs' Day. Observed on Sept. 30, one day before National Day, the day commemorates those who gave their lives for national independence and prosperity. Since Martyrs' Day was established in 2014, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, has maintained the tradition of paying homage to fallen heroes on the day. The other leaders who attended the ceremony on Wednesday included Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng. They were joined by representatives from all walks of life. At 10 a.m., all attendees sang the national anthem, followed by a moment of silence in tribute to the heroes who sacrificed their lives for the liberation of the Chinese people and the development of the People's Republic of China. Nine large flower baskets were placed in front of the Monument to the People's Heroes. Xi and other leaders walked up to the foot of the monument, where he straightened the ribbons on the baskets. Then, they walked around the monument to pay their tributes. The baskets, with ribbons reading "Eternal Glory to the People's Heroes," were presented in the name of the CPC Central Committee; the National People's Congress Standing Committee; the State Council; the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference; the Central Military Commission; non-Communist parties, the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce, and patriots without party affiliations; people's organizations and people from all walks of life; veterans, retired senior officials and the relatives of martyrs; and Chinese Young Pioneers. Yin Li, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and secretary of the CPC Beijing Municipal Committee, presided over the ceremony. This year marks the 105th founding anniversary of the CPC and the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, which lasted from 1934 to 1936. item.title: China extends trade barrier probes into U.S. actions to Dec. 27
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- China's commerce ministry has extended its trade barrier investigations into U.S. actions and measures which harm global production and supply chains as well as impede trading of green products, citing the complexity of the cases. The investigations, launched on March 27, have been extended until Dec. 27, in accordance with the rules on foreign trade barrier investigations, the Ministry of Commerce (MOC) said on Wednesday. The ministry said in March that the investigations covered U.S. practices and measures that may gravely harm the trade interests of Chinese enterprises, with some potentially violating World Trade Organization rules and other economic and trade treaties or agreements jointly concluded or participated in by China and the United States. Preliminary evidence and information obtained by the MOC indicate that these practices and measures include, but are not limited to, restricting or banning the export of high-tech products to China, curbing bilateral investment in key sectors, restricting exports of green products to the United States, delaying deployment of new energy projects, and limiting technological cooperation related to green products, according to the statements in March. ■

item.title: China's September PMIs return to expansion amid firming recovery
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- China's manufacturing activity was back in expansion territory in September while non-manufacturing activity rebounded markedly, with both above the boom-bust line, official data showed on Wednesday, adding to signs of a firming recovery in the world's second-largest economy. The purchasing managers' index (PMI) for China's manufacturing sector stood at 50.1 in September 2026, up 0.3 percentage points from August and returning to the expansion zone, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). A reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signifies contraction. The manufacturing sector's business climate improved further in September, with the PMI rising for a second consecutive month, said Huo Lihui, a chief statistician with the NBS. Among the 21 industries surveyed, 12 reported a PMI above the expansion threshold, four more than the previous month, Huo noted. The sector saw expansion in both manufacturing output and market demand in September. The production sub-index climbed to 51.7, up 1.3 percentage points from August, while the new orders index was at 50.5, still above the threshold. Driven by the acceleration in production, enterprises' willingness to purchase strengthened, with the procurement volume index reaching 51.0, an increase of 0.5 percentage points from the previous month, said Huo. PMIs for the equipment manufacturing industry, the high-tech manufacturing industry and the consumer goods industry stood at 51, 52.5 and 50.7, respectively, all remaining in the expansion zone. Affected by rising international commodity prices and growing demand in some industries, the purchasing price index for major raw materials and the ex-factory price index for manufacturing stood at 60.8 and 54, respectively, up 4.2 percentage points and 3.6 percentage points from the previous month. PMIs for medium-sized and small manufacturing enterprises came in at 49.7 and 48.9, respectively, increases of 0.3 percentage points and 1 percentage point from the previous month, as business activity picked up. Non-manufacturing activity also increased. The business activity index for the non-manufacturing sector reached 50.2 in September, a rise of 1.2 percentage points from August. The construction sector index rose 3.4 percentage points to 50.3, the highest level this year, while the services sector index increased by 0.9 percentage points to 50.2, with both returning to expansion. "The traditional peak season and the upcoming National Day holiday have driven up demand in transportation, tourism and related consumer services," said Wu Wei, an analyst with the China Logistics Information Center. The improvement came as a package of pro-growth measures was rolled out at a faster pace. The National Development and Reform Commission on Wednesday said it, together with the Ministry of Finance, had allocated the fourth and final batch of 62.5 billion yuan (around 9.28 billion U.S. dollars) in ultra-long special treasury bonds for consumer goods trade-in programs, bringing this year's total to 250 billion yuan. Starting Oct. 1, China will implement interest subsidies for housing loans for eligible first-home buyers, offering an annualized subsidy of 1 percentage point on loans of up to 1 million yuan for up to five years, the Ministry of Finance and other departments said. The People's Bank of China, China's central bank, announced a raft of strengthened support measures on Tuesday, including cutting the one-year interest rate of the pledged supplementary lending (PSL) facility from 1.75 percent to 1.5 percent, to better incentivize policy banks to support the real economy and serve national strategies. It has also decided to increase the quota of the relending facility for sci-tech innovation and technological upgrades by 200 billion yuan and for agriculture and small and micro businesses by 500 billion yuan, out of which 300 billion yuan is dedicated to financial support for private firms. "The recent policy mix is characterized by stepped-up counter-cyclical adjustments and the concentrated rollout of incremental tools," said Wen Bin, chief economist with China Minsheng Bank. "With existing policies becoming more effective and incremental policies continuing to be introduced, economic momentum is expected to pick up further in the fourth quarter," he noted. Looking ahead, China's manufacturing sector is expected to maintain steady and moderate expansion in the fourth quarter, said Wen Tao, an analyst with the China Logistics Information Center, citing accelerated implementation of major projects, including about 2 trillion yuan of planned investment by central state-owned enterprises in six major infrastructure networks this year. ■

item.title: Xi, Brunei's Sultan exchange congratulations on 35th anniversary of ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Sultan of Brunei Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Mu'izzaddin Waddaulah on Wednesday exchanged congratulations on the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. Xi noted that the traditional friendship between China and Brunei has a long history and remained strong over time. In the process of working together towards modernization, the two countries have set an example of mutual respect, equality and common development between large and small countries, Xi added. Over the 35 years since the establishment of diplomatic ties, China and Brunei have steadily deepened political mutual trust, achieved fruitful results in cooperation across various fields, and strengthened people-to-people exchanges, he said. Xi said that last year, Hassanal paid a state visit to China, during which the two sides reached important consensus on building a China-Brunei community with a shared future, ushering bilateral relations into a new stage of historical development. Xi emphasized that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Brunei relations and is willing to work with Hassanal to take the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties as an opportunity to carry forward traditional friendship, enhance the alignment of development strategies, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, and advance the building of the China-Brunei community with a shared future in a more substantive and in-depth manner, so as to better benefit the two peoples and contribute more to regional prosperity and stability. Hassanal stated that over the past 35 years since establishing diplomatic relations, Brunei and China have consistently trusted, respected, and understood each other. In 2025, the two countries reached an important consensus on building a community with a shared future, he added. He looks forward to taking the 35th anniversary of Brunei-China diplomatic relations as an opportunity to further strengthen bilateral ties, deepen cooperation and exchanges in areas such as economy, trade, investment, defense, and culture, and jointly achieve prosperity and progress for both countries, thereby better benefiting their peoples. ■

item.title: Xi calls for firm confidence, solid steps for China's national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech at a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on the nation to forge ahead with firm confidence and take solid steps to achieve the great national rejuvenation. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a reception held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. China's National Day falls on Oct. 1. Li Qiang presided over the reception. Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attended the event along with around 800 guests. "The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is unstoppable," Xi said. "As long as we remain confident, stay focused on our goals and move forward steadily, step by step, success will ultimately belong to the great CPC, the great Chinese people and the great People's Republic of China." He noted that over the past 77 years, the Party has led the Chinese people in achieving two miracles: rapid economic growth and enduring social stability. "We take immense pride in the extraordinary achievements of New China and have full confidence in the bright prospects of Chinese modernization," he said. Since the beginning of this year, the Chinese economy has continued to progress despite mounting pressure and achieved innovation-driven and high-quality development, demonstrating strong resilience and vitality, he said. Efforts should be made to sustain this momentum, promote innovation-driven, high-quality and sound economic development, take practical steps to safeguard and improve people's livelihoods, and meet the targets and tasks set for the year, so as to ensure a good start to the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), he said. Xi stressed the need to remain firmly committed to the policy of "one country, two systems," under which the people of Hong Kong administer Hong Kong, the people of Macao administer Macao, and both regions enjoy a high degree of autonomy. He went on to say that the central government will support Hong Kong and Macao in integrating more fully into the country's overall development. The central government is committed to maintaining their long-term prosperity and stability, Xi added. He also called for efforts to deepen exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait, resolutely fight secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," oppose external interference, and promote the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations to advance national reunification.
